---
chapter: 1
title: The Last Full Cut
pov: Odile
story_date: January 1929
status: draft
words: 318
---

The pond rang under the horse before it rang under the saws. Odile heard it from the
scale house doorway, a long note that came up through the boards and the soles of her
boots, and she wrote the time in the green book before she wrote anything else.

Marcel had marked the grid at first light. Twenty-two inch squares, the lines scored
with the plow and the plow horse walking them the way she walked the aisle at church,
head down, unhurried. By eight o'clock the first raft of cakes was floating in the
channel and the men were poling it toward the water door.

Wilfred came up the ramp with frost in three days of beard. "Four thousand ton," he
said. "We fill her this year."

"You'll fill her." Odile did not look up from the column.

"Sprague will take what the cannery takes."

"He will."

She had the letter in the drawer under the route slips. Half the summer order, set
down in a clerk's hand and signed by Ezra Sprague, who had been polite about it, who
had asked after her mother's eyes. Four thousand tons of ice would go into the pond
house and something under two thousand would come out of it, and the rest would run
down the hill in July as water.

The hoist chain took up. A cake came out of the channel streaming, blue at the core
where the pond had frozen slow, and swung in over the sawdust while a man walked it
around with a hook.

"Weigh it," Wilfred said.

Odile put the beam on the platform and set the poise and read the number off the bar,
and she wrote three hundred and four pounds in the green book in a hand that did not
shake at all.
